population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 23.5% − current 15.0% = 8.5% of adults (≈22.7M) used and are off now. ≈6.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈2.0 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (6.0+2.0)/23.5 = 34% cycled. The figure is down from 40% because about 7.0 pts of adults started for the first time in 2029–30 and are still on their first course; one-year persistence of ~35% and restart of 36–47% still describe earlier cohorts. Current users ≈ 40.0M of ~267M adults. Age check: 0.20×6.5 + 0.33×15 + 0.24×25 + 0.23×12 ≈ 15.0. The growth comes from public expansion. The Part D obesity benefit (Jan 2030) and the 75% enhanced Medicaid match brought in older and low-income adults, and the HRSA free oral programme reached ~2.0M uninsured people. That is why the bottom third rose from 6.5% to 11.5%, the fastest of any group. 65+ use went from 8% to 12% (~7.4M of ~62M) even with the bone label, because the new benefit bundles DEXA and strength counselling, which reassured prescribers. The income gradient in who uses has narrowed; the gradient in which drug, at what dose and with what monitoring has widened. Off-drug people: ~22.7M stopped, ~2M of them are 65+ women who stopped on DEXA results, and ~204M never used. The never-users are now concentrated in uninsured working-age adults above 200% FPL in non-opt-in states (12 states, including Texas, Florida and Georgia), and in adults 18–29. Pediatric: ~0.6% of under-18s (≈440k), mostly adolescents 12+ on oral semaglutide. Off-label use for 'screen compulsion' in teens is reported and contested. No child has more than ~7 years of exposure, and adolescent bone-accrual data are still pending.

access.public_coverage: Public programmes are now the largest payer: ≈47.5% of incretin users. MEDICARE (20%, ≈8.0M: ~7.4M aged 65+ plus ~0.6M disabled). The Sep 2029 reconciliation act lifted the Part D statutory exclusion for anti-obesity drugs from Jan 2030 and wrote the Bridge rate into law as a ceiling: Medicare pays ~$245/month and the beneficiary pays a $50 copay. Criteria widened to BMI≥27 with any one comorbidity, prediabetes included, and the act requires baseline DEXA and a strength-counselling visit for 65+. Obesity-indication Medicare users ≈3.6M × $245 × 12 = $10.6B/yr federal; the rest is Part D diabetes use. MEDICAID (22.5%, ≈9.0M) at the same $245 rate; 38 states plus DC opted into the new 75% enhanced match for obesity coverage. The ≈6.0M on the obesity indication cost 6.0M × $245 × 12 = $17.6B/yr, of which ≈$13.2B is federal (75%). The ≈3.0M on the diabetes indication are paid at regular FMAP. The Indiana and Arkansas adherence-gated waivers remain in force. HRSA METABOLIC ACCESS PROGRAM (5%, ≈2.0M uninsured/underinsured adults under 200% FPL through FQHCs) provides free oral semaglutide or Foundayo, bought at a negotiated $149/month flat across doses: 2.0M × $149 × 12 = $3.6B/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 70+ generic semaglutide brands, injectable and oral, at $8–45/month. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 75–110. Generics also in Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China. Generic oral semaglutide is sold in ~180 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32, and generic-entry litigation is pending.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~40.0M users: commercial 33% (13.2M), Medicare 20% (8.0M), Medicaid 22.5% (9.0M), HRSA free provision 5% (2.0M), cash/direct 14.5% (5.8M), gray/imported 5% (2.0M); total 100% = 40.0M. Prices are stalled. TrumpRx/direct cash is still ~$245–350 for injectables and $149 for oral starting doses. Wegovy lists at $1,349 and retatrutide at $1,499. Oral amycretin (Jul 2029) lists at $1,299 with a $499 direct-cash price and no TrumpRx tier. Prices stay put because demand now exceeds supply: an oral peptide needs many times the API of a weekly injection, so public-programme volume competes with cash buyers for the same tablets. Manufacturers ration high-dose orals by channel. FDA has declined to declare a shortage because injectable supply is adequate, which keeps compounding closed. About 54% of current users are on daily orals, including nearly all HRSA patients and most new Medicaid starts; the affluent skew toward injectable retatrutide or oral amycretin. Employers drifted from 58% to 56% coverage. Some smaller firms dropped coverage and pointed early retirees and low-wage staff toward Medicaid and HRSA. Adherence-gated PBM programmes remain at ~40% of covering employers, but PDC measures fills, not tablets swallowed.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Mar 2028)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Jan 2029)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral and weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Jul 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: MASH / liver (semaglutide; survodutide label includes MASH data)
smoking cessation adjunct to varenicline/NRT (oral semaglutide, approved Apr 2029)
gambling disorder, adjunct to counselling, adults (oral semaglutide, approved May 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: compulsive shopping and compulsive sexual behaviour, prescribed via telehealth on the strength of the gambling label
'screen' or gaming compulsion in adolescents and young adults; contested, and the AAP advises against it
low-dose 'metabolic health' / longevity use by people without obesity, mostly in the top income third
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Survodutide was approved Jan 2029 from its Oct 2027 filing; uptake is modest outside hepatology. Amycretin's Jun 2028 NDA covered daily oral and weekly injectable forms, and FDA approved it Jul 2029, 13 months after filing. The oral delivers ~22% mean loss at 68 weeks, matching tirzepatide. This is the 'oral parity' moment: a pill now equals the leading injectable, though not retatrutide's 28%. Supply is the binding constraint. Oral semaglutide picked up smoking cessation (Apr 2029) and gambling disorder (May 2030). The gambling sNDA was filed Sep 2029 on a phase 3 trial running since 2027 and got priority review, since no drug was approved for the condition. MariTide (monthly) is still in phase 3, with filing expected 2031; it is not on the market. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not approved. No US generic semaglutide or tirzepatide. The incretin market is ≈$140B in 2030: US volume up ~50%, US prices flat, and the HRSA flat price plus ex-US generics pulling the average down.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin titration has GI rates similar to injectables. Daily-oral 'weekend skipping' produces re-titration nausea on Mondays, which clinicians describe.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute case counts rising with the user base.
No causal confirmation in larger long-term data; absolute risk low.

Unchanged in size: ~1.5× sarcopenia criteria in 65+ users on >2 years. The absolute number affected is rising with 65+ use at 12%. Lean-mass share of loss is ~25–40%; it is lower in users with supervised resistance training, who skew affluent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028). The 2029 act makes a strength-counselling visit a condition of Part D obesity coverage for 65+.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users, concentrated in women and in cyclers. No new signal; follow-up cohorts confirm without enlarging it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling; DEXA required at baseline for Part D obesity coverage in 65+. The Senate HELP report (2029) referred Novo disclosure questions to DOJ, and civil settlement talks are ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; gambling-disorder trial psychiatric monitoring found no signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning absent from US labels since Jan 2026; unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide postmarketing anhedonia-scale interim data (2029) and new surveys are consistent with the earlier ~10–15% of long-term users reporting reduced pleasure, dose-dependent. No validated causal estimate. The gambling-disorder label describes the mechanism as therapeutic.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No warning. FDA asked for anhedonia scales in amycretin and gambling-indication postmarketing studies. The gambling label recommends dose review if patients report loss of interest in non-target activities.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year of stopping. Involuntary stops from Indiana/Arkansas gating and employer lapses continue, and voluntary partial stops (dose holidays) produce smaller oscillations.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation is ongoing; a district court let it proceed (2029). The 2029 act bars enhanced-match states from imposing new lockouts longer than 6 months but grandfathers existing waivers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals persist for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein, most visible in low-income oral users without dietitian access.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the HRSA programme includes a multivitamin in its kit.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist. The cycling-and-bone question is unresolved, and adolescent bone-accrual studies are enrolling with no readout.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric bone-accrual studies required.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Harms come from imported and counterfeit pens and, increasingly, counterfeit 'oral amycretin' tablets sold online. Poison-centre calls are roughly flat as HRSA and Medicaid absorb some former gray buyers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion final; import alerts; FDA warning letters to online tablet sellers.

food_and_beverage.state: With users up by half, volume pressure is accelerating again. US packaged-snack and confectionery volumes are down ~3–4%/yr, and the declines are now concentrated in discount and dollar channels, where Medicaid and HRSA users shop. Big Food portfolios have shifted further into protein, dairy, fibre and smaller packs. Private-label protein is the fastest-growing grocery line in low-income zip codes.

alcohol.state: Still contracting. The gambling label and cessation indication have given 'craving' drugs mainstream legitimacy. Beer is hit hardest in blue-collar markets because Medicaid uptake is new there. Spirits are premiumising. Sportsbooks report softer handle growth in Ohio and New Jersey and name GLP-1 prescribing as a risk factor for the first time.

restaurants.state: Traffic holds. Small plates and protein-forward menus are universal. Value-volume chains in high-Medicaid-uptake counties now underperform the way suburban buffets did in 2028. 'Off-dose Friday' promotions appear at bars.

apparel.state: Plus-size is shrinking again as low-income uptake rises. The premium market has moved to fitted 'shape' clothing that shows arms and shoulders: sleeveless workwear and structured tees. Mass retailers sell loose, size-fluid basics.

fitness.state: Growing and stratifying. Boutique strength studios with DEXA packages ($250–400/month) cluster in affluent zip codes. Part D strength-counselling visits have spawned low-cost MA and YMCA 'bone classes'. A coached physique is now a purchased good.

insurance.state: Public programmes now carry ~47.5% of incretin users. Commercial plans hold coverage at 56% of employers and keep adherence gating and BMI-linked surcharges. Some employers quietly steer low-wage staff to Medicaid/HRSA. Commercial pharmacy trend is ~+7%.

pharma.state: Volume is supply-constrained, and US prices are flat by choice and by capacity. Novo has partly recovered on oral amycretin despite DOJ exposure; Lilly leads on retatrutide and Foundayo. Ex-US generics erode foreign revenue. API and oral-peptide capacity build-outs in North Carolina and Denmark are the capital theme.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug no longer marks class: one adult in seven is on it, including home-health aides and line cooks on Medicaid pills. What marks class is what the body looks like after losing weight. Defined shoulders, grip and upright posture signal a coach, a DEXA scan and a retatrutide or amycretin script. Thin with soft, narrow arms and slack skin signals a free pill and no supervision. The slang 'kiosk thin' (from the Indiana scales) and 'built' are in common use.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The usage gap narrowed: top third 18% versus bottom third 11.5%. The body gap moved to muscle. In North Dallas, women 40–60 in finance and insurance go to strength studios that bundle quarterly DEXA, and visible deltoids are an office norm. In Cleveland's east side and Parma, Ohio Medicaid and HRSA clinics have put home-health aides and nursing-home staff, a largely female workforce, on oral semaglutide in large numbers. They lose weight on 12-hour shifts with no protein budget and no time to train. Both groups are thinner; only one looks it in the way that is read as success.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and protein comes first, at every income level. Weekend dose skipping lets people 'eat for real' at birthdays and Sunday dinners, so the family table has regained an appetite on Saturdays.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On/off' filters remain on apps. Affluent users list 'trained' or post DEXA numbers. Couples schedule dose holidays around anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still something to manage. The new norm is managing it intermittently: dampen it on weekdays and allow it back on weekends. Having no appetite at all is starting to read as a dose problem rather than a virtue.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Measured prevalence is unchanged at ~10–15% of long-term users reporting reduced pleasure, dose-dependent, with interim retatrutide anhedonia-scale data consistent. It moved from niche to mainstream complaint because the base widened to 40M people, the gambling label made the mechanism explicit, and daily pills made adjustment easy. Surveys suggest roughly a third of oral users skip doses deliberately at least monthly. 'The flat' is ordinary vocabulary.
interior_life.framing: Called 'the flat' when complained about, 'reward modulation' in clinic, and 'treatment' on the gambling and cessation labels. Wellness vendors have dropped 'even-keel' marketing to HR after union pushback. The prevailing frame is now dosing literacy: everyone is expected to know their own number.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Logistics and DOT-regulated driving still favour staying on, since sleep-apnea clearance depends on it. A Teamsters master contract (2030) bars PBMs from sending dose-change or skip data to employers and protects 'medically supervised dose adjustment'. Sales staff and creatives openly titrate down. Managers learn not to ask about Mondays.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is a genre label: songwriters credit tracks recorded on holiday weeks, and comics do 'Saturday sets'. Casinos and sportsbooks see more weekend-concentrated play. Ohio's sports-betting tax now partly funds gambling-disorder prescriptions, and comics have noticed.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is a common, unembarrassing complaint. Dose holidays timed around sex and travel are routine. Sex therapists and couples counsellors ask about dose and skip days at intake.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Visible in coverage and price politics, and in a new argument over whether the state is subsidising quietness. Some progressive and libertarian commentators question giving free reward-dampening pills to low-wage workers. Disability and poor people's campaigns answer that the affluent have had the drugs for years. No measurable change in turnout or protest behaviour is established.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and pro-speed: survodutide, oral amycretin, and the cessation and gambling indications were all approved. Defensive on bone and muscle, with DEXA and counselling written into coverage law. The agency refuses to declare a shortage of rationed orals, which keeps compounding closed. Selective enforcement on imports.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The Sep 2029 reconciliation act ended the Part D exclusion at a $245 payment ceiling with a $50 copay, created a 75% enhanced Medicaid match for obesity coverage (38 states plus DC opted in), and funded the HRSA Metabolic Access Program, which gives free orals to ~2.0M low-income uninsured adults through FQHCs at $149/month federal cost. Combined new federal obesity outlays ≈ $10.6B (Medicare) + $13.2B (Medicaid federal share) + $3.6B (HRSA) ≈ $27.4B/yr.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas gated waivers are grandfathered. The act caps new lockouts at 6 months in enhanced-match states but permits quarterly weigh-ins. Pharmacy-kiosk weigh-ins have spread to 9 states. Employer BMI surcharges up to 30% remain legal. HRSA requires clinic weigh-ins every 6 months. Daily orals make actual ingestion unverifiable, which undercuts all adherence metrics.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto requirement for some drivers. The Army permits GLP-1 use for accession and is now piloting oral semaglutide for soldiers who fail body-composition tests, which is contested in Congress.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Prices are stalled against $8–45 Indian generics. Section 232 tariffs and oral-peptide API capacity are the manufacturers' stated reasons. India–US talks include a personal-import tolerance quota proposal, still unsigned. High-dose oral supply is allocated to US public contracts first, and European payers complain.

events.event: FDA approves Novo Nordisk's amycretin as a daily pill and a weekly injection; the oral delivers ~22% mean weight loss at 68 weeks, matching tirzepatide. List price $1,299, direct cash $499, no TrumpRx tier, supply allocated by channel

Reconciliation act lifts Medicare Part D's anti-obesity drug exclusion from Jan 2030 at a $245 payment ceiling and $50 copay, with DEXA and strength-counselling requirements for 65+, and creates a 75% enhanced Medicaid match for obesity coverage; 38 states and DC opt in by late 2030

HRSA launches the Metabolic Access Program: free oral semaglutide or Foundayo through community health centres for uninsured adults under 200% FPL, bought at a negotiated $149 a month; enrolment passes 2 million by October

Lilly and Novo keep all US cash and TrumpRx prices unchanged for a fourth year, citing oral-peptide API limits and tariffs; FDA declines to list high-dose orals as in shortage, keeping compounders shut out

FDA approves oral semaglutide as an adjunct for gambling disorder in adults, the first drug for the condition; Ohio announces sports-betting tax revenue will fund treatment, and telehealth prescribing for compulsive shopping and sexual behaviour follows within weeks

Teamsters ratify a freight contract barring PBMs from reporting dose changes or skipped doses to employers and protecting 'medically supervised dose adjustment', after a year in which 'the flat' and weekend dose holidays became talk-show material

open_tensions: The state now pays for nearly half of incretin users and is the main reason the bottom third is on the drug, but it pays for pills, not for muscle. Coached physiques remain a private purchase, so the subsidy narrows the use gap while widening the body gap, in a population already carrying the bone and sarcopenia label.

Demand exceeds oral-peptide supply at stalled prices. Public contracts and cash buyers compete for the same tablets, FDA's refusal to declare a shortage keeps compounding closed, and a significant gray market fills the gap at $8–45 a month.

Daily pills have made adherence metrics unverifiable just as Medicaid waivers, PBMs and the HRSA programme depend on them, and weekend dose holidays are now normal behaviour that the gating rules count as non-adherence only if fills lapse.

The gambling label makes reward modulation an approved therapy while the same effect is the country's commonest complaint about the drug. Free provision to low-wage workers raises an unanswered question: is the state treating compulsion, or subsidising quiet?
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Medicare pays ~$245 a month for an incretin, with a ~$50 beneficiary copay (now in statute rather than under the Bridge demonstration).
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: One in Seven Americans Is On It, and Washington Pays. Now Class Shows in Your Arms
prose.world_in_600_words:
In late 2030 about forty million American adults, roughly one in seven, take an incretin drug, and the federal government pays for more of them than anyone else does. Two years ago the drugs looked like a perk of good insurance. Then a budget bill quietly ended Medicare's old ban on paying for weight-loss medicines and kept the price at the $245 a month Medicare had already been paying. The same bill offered states three federal dollars for every one they spent on covering the drugs in Medicaid. Thirty-eight states and Washington, DC said yes. A separate programme now hands out free daily pills at community health centres to about two million uninsured people. The poorest third of the country used to take these drugs at half the rate of the richest. The gap is smaller now and still closing.

The pill made most of that possible. In July 2029 Novo Nordisk won approval for a daily tablet that works about as well as the leading weekly injection. For many people the needle had been the last reason not to start, and it no longer is. Just over half of users now take a pill. The catch is that pills use far more raw drug than injections, and there isn't enough to go around. Prices have not moved in four years. Cash buyers pay what they paid in 2027. Novo's new pill sells for $499 a month to those who can get it. Manufacturers decide which channel gets the tablets, and the government's own contracts come first. Indian pharmacies still mail generic versions for the price of lunch, and about two million Americans still order them.

There is no new safety alarm, and the old ones still stand. Long-term users over sixty-five lose bone and muscle faster than their peers. The new Medicare benefit therefore requires a bone scan before the first prescription and a visit to discuss strength training. For most retirees that visit is a pamphlet and a bone-health class at the YMCA. For people who can afford more, it is a $300-a-month strength studio with quarterly body scans and a coach.

That difference is how class now shows. Thinness no longer tells anyone much, because a home-health aide in Parma, Ohio is as likely to be on a pill as a bank executive in North Dallas. What tells is shoulders, grip and posture. In Dallas offices, toned arms are part of the dress code. On Cleveland's east side, women working twelve-hour shifts have lost weight with no protein budget and no time to train. They are thinner, and soft, and people have started calling it 'kiosk thin'.

The other change is in what people say out loud. The drugs dull appetite for food, and for drink, cigarettes and bets. This spring the FDA approved oral semaglutide for gambling disorder, the first drug for the condition. Ohio, which legalised sports betting, will use betting tax revenue to pay for it. Telehealth companies were soon prescribing for compulsive shopping. Yet the same quieting effect, which most people call 'the flat', is the commonest complaint about the drugs. Surveys say a third of pill users skip doses on purpose, usually at weekends, to taste a birthday cake or feel a concert. The freight contract the Teamsters ratified in August forbids pharmacy-benefit managers from telling employers about skipped doses. Adherence-tracking programmes count refills, and nobody can count which pills get swallowed.

From the outside the country looks healthier and calmer. Sleep apnea is down, beer sales are down and plus-size racks are shrinking again. The question nobody in Washington has answered is what exactly it is buying, at about $27 billion a year: treatment for compulsion, or a quieter workforce.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk takes her pill at 5:40 with a glass of water and nothing else, standing at the counter. It's on Ohio Medicaid, and the copay is three dollars she never notices.

At Mr. Halloran's she lifts him from the bed to the chair, his arm thin as a broom handle against her own arm. His DEXA report is magneted to the fridge beside a printout headed BONE HEALTH: 3 THINGS. His daughter flew in from Plano last night. She is maybe fifty, in a sleeveless top, her arms ropey and tan. She asks Denise what she's on. "The regular," Denise says. The daughter nods and says she does the new pill, the hard-to-get one, plus a coach. "You should lift," she says, kindly. Denise is already lifting a hundred and sixty pounds of man.

Lunch is a protein shake from the Dollar General, store brand, vanilla.

After the second client she sits in the Corolla and checks the app her brother-in-law Rick sent her, a sportsbook. Rick got a prescription in June, the gambling one. He says he still watches the Browns but doesn't feel the game in his stomach anymore. He said it like a man describing a quiet house.

Tomorrow is Saturday, and her granddaughter Kaylee turns seven. Denise sets the pill bottle on the windowsill instead of beside the coffee maker. That's how she remembers to skip.

She wants to taste the cake. She wants to be hungry for it.

Monday she'll be sick for a morning. Everybody is.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weekend dose skipping lets people 'eat for real' at birthdays and Sunday dinners, so the family table has regained an appetite on Saturdays.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: oral semaglutide has a roughly week-long half-life, and the other daily orals also persist beyond a day. Skipping one or two doses should barely restore appetite, let alone cause 're-titration nausea on Mondays'. The central cultural shift is asserted without a plausible pharmacological chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: bought at a negotiated $149/month flat across doses: 2.0M × $149 × 12 = $3.6B/yr
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world says high-dose oral supply is binding and rationed by channel, yet manufacturers sell all doses to HRSA at $149, well below the $499 direct-cash price of amycretin. No reason is given why scarce tablets would go to the cheapest buyer at a flat price.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The gambling sNDA was filed Sep 2029 on a phase 3 trial running since 2027 and got priority review, since no drug was approved for the condition.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: approval in May 2030 comes about 8 months after filing, inside the 12-month minimum for a phase 3 asset. The 2028 world also called gambling use 'still anecdotal', so a phase 3 running since 2027 appears from nowhere.

rationale.badness: Access broadens and the use gap narrows, so the median person is not clearly worse off. The harms are structural and quiet: a bone and sarcopenia burden in 7.4M adults 65+, the body gap (muscle versus 'kiosk thin'), 'the flat' as an ordinary complaint, and BMI surcharges and gated waivers persisting. Adherence data are unverifiable with daily pills, and the anhedonia harm is still unmeasured while the state subsidises it. That is a recognisably harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible and traceable to fields and events, including adoption (+5.1), stalled prices, public expansion, gambling approval, oral parity, class stratification, the HRSA subsidy, and mainstream complaint. Safety and market shock stay at none. mechanism: Public expansion producing the bottom-third rise is well shown, but weekend skipping (claim 1) is pharmacologically doubtful and the flat $149 HRSA price under rationing (claim 2) is unexplained. Part D and Medicaid ramps are also fast. magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope, and the payer mix, cycling arithmetic, age check and $27.4B budget all reconcile. The gambling approval about 8 months after filing breaks the 12-month rule (claim 3), and the smoking indication is roughly 11 months after the May 2028 filing.
rationale.generativity: The world and prose give strong characters and scenes: Denise, the Plano daughter, the pill bottle on the windowsill, Rick's 'quiet house', the Dollar General shake. Details like 'kiosk thin', 'off-dose Friday', Saturday sets, and Teamsters bargaining over skip data add texture. Cleveland and Dallas contrast, a ready film setting, and the day-in-the-life shows more than it explains.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The gambling sNDA was filed Sep 2029 on a phase 3 trial running since 2027 and got priority review, since no drug was approved for the condition.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the envelope allows approval of a phase 3 product no earlier than 12 months after filing, and this one is approved May 2030, 8 months after a Sep 2029 filing. The trial 'running since 2027' is invented, since the 2028 world called gambling use only anecdotal. The smoking-cessation sNDA, filed May 2028 and approved Apr 2029, is also 11 months.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Weekend dose skipping lets people 'eat for real' at birthdays and Sunday dinners, so the family table has regained an appetite on Saturdays.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: oral semaglutide, which most Medicaid and HRSA users take, has a roughly week-long half-life, so skipping a weekend would barely change drug levels. The appetite release and the Monday re-titration nausea ('Everybody is') are asserted without a pharmacological chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: bought at a negotiated $149/month flat across doses: 2.0M × $149 × 12 = $3.6B/yr.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world says oral-peptide supply is binding and manufacturers ration high-dose orals by channel, yet they sell to a free programme at a flat starting-dose price across all doses. HRSA also reaches 2M enrolees within ten months of launch, with no chain showing why suppliers would accept this.

least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: oral semaglutide has a roughly week-long half-life, and the other daily orals also persist beyond a day. No reason is given why scarce tablets would go to the cheapest buyer at a flat price.

rationale.badness: Access broadens and the use gap narrows, so the median person is not clearly worse off.
